subject: Clarifying default retention: requests vs generated outputs (BrightBank, EU residency)
messages:
From: Anna Kowalski <anna.kowalski@brightbank.com>

Subject: Retention / residency question for PoC

Hi Connor,

Quick question as we're finalising the PoC scope: by default, what exactly does Redwood retain for a request served via the hosted API? Specifically we need to clarify: 1) whether full prompts and user inputs are persisted; 2) whether model outputs (the generated text) are kept separately; 3) do partial streamed tokens/partial responses get stored; and 4) how does residency work for EU customers — are both requests and outputs stored in EU-only storage by default or is there any U.S. ingress?

Also, if we wanted an automatic purge after X days, how is that requested and what is the SLA for a complete purge? We have to present this to our legal/security folks tomorrow.

Thanks — appreciate a concise breakdown.

Best,
Anna
Anna Kowalski
Head of Platform Risk, BrightBank

Hi Anna —

Thanks for the clear list. Looping in Kimberly (Product & Privacy) to confirm a compact, customer-friendly answer and Marissa (Support/Compliance) for purge process detail.

I can start with a short summary and will follow up with the official guidance doc:
- By default we capture request metadata (timestamps, model id, routing info) and the full request payload (prompts/user inputs) for a limited retention period.
- Generated outputs are stored as artifacts distinct from the raw request, and are subject to the same default retention window unless the customer opts into stricter policies.
- Streamed partial tokens: we do not persist intermediate streaming frames as separate persisted artifacts; only the final reconstructed output is retained when applicable.
- EU residency: for accounts provisioned in EU regions, both requests and stored outputs are kept in EU storage by default; there is no asynchronous U.S. ingress for persisted artifacts unless cross-region routing is explicitly enabled.

Kimberly / Marissa — can you confirm retention window numbers and the purge SLA? Anna — I'll deliver a short, plain-English guidance and attach a sample purge request form.

Connor

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>

Date: Fri, 2 Oct 2026 12:15:00 +0100
Subject: Re: Retention / residency question for PoC

Connor — adding specifics below (keeps concise for the customer deck):

1) What we store by default
- Request payloads (prompts, user inputs): retained for 45 days by default for hosted accounts; that includes the full prompt and any attached metadata such as client-provided IDs.
- Model outputs (generated text): retained 45 days by default, stored as separate artifacts.
- Streaming behavior: intermediate token frames used to assemble a streaming response are transient in-memory only; we persist the final output artifact only.
- Embeddings / derivative artifacts: embeddings are treated as generated artifacts and follow the same 45-day default unless otherwise configured.

2) Residency
- EU-provisioned accounts: all persisted artifacts (requests and outputs) are stored on EU-only storage. No default cross-border replication.
- Customers can opt into cross-region replication (e.g., EU -> US) which will be explicit in the config and contract.

3) Purge / deletion requests
- Self-service: customers with admin access can request on-demand deletion through the Console (Data > Artifacts > Purge).
- Manual compliance purge: for a full account-level purge, submit a signed purge request; typical SLA for completing a complete purge is 72 hours for hosted accounts.
- Audit trail: every purge action is logged and a confirmation bundle is returned (log id + manifest).

Attachments: I attached a short retention matrix and the purge request template (for legal).

Let me know if you want this condensed further for legal.

-Kim

Connor / Kim — adding a few operational caveats that customers commonly ask about:

- Backups & disaster recovery: backups of persisted artifacts are kept for an additional 7 days beyond the active retention window to support recovery; these backups are subject to the same residency rules (EU backups in EU). Note: we do not use backups for analytics purposes.
- Logs vs artifacts: telemetry logs (scheduling, infra-level traces) are retained per our telemetry TTL (default 90 days) and are not considered user artifacts; they do not contain full prompt text by default unless debug mode is enabled.
- Exemptions: certain support investigations may require temporary extension of retention for a small subset of artifacts; this requires customer approval and is timeboxed and auditable.

I also included example language customers can use in contracts: short bullet points that legal teams prefer.

Marissa

Anna —

Thanks for the prompt. Attached is a short summary and sample purge form for your legal/security team. Short takeaway you can paste into the deck: 

- By default Redwood retains both requests (prompts/inputs) and final generated outputs for 45 days for hosted accounts. Derivatives like embeddings follow the same default.
- Streaming intermediate tokens are not persisted; only the final output artifact is stored.
- EU accounts store persisted artifacts in EU-only storage by default; there is no U.S. replication unless explicitly configured.
- Self-service purge available in Console; for account-level signed purge requests we complete the purge within 72 hours and return an audit manifest.

If legal wants more formal contract wording or an exportable evidence pack (SOC2 excerpts, retention matrix) let us know and we'll open a formal evidence request.
